note: FNS Section 1063 is a QC variance determination procedure, not a caseworker policy requirement. It falls under '1060 VARIANCE DETERMINATIONS' and prescribes how Quality Control reviewers must evaluate the accuracy of earned income budgeting in prospectively budgeted cases — including how QC must handle averaged vs non-averaged income, how to treat vacation/sick pay in the error determination process, when to use Section 722 for new/terminated sources, and how to distinguish reported from unreported income sources (routing to 1063.1, 1063.2, 1063.3). These are audit methodology instructions for QC reviewers, not policy rules that caseworkers implement. The underlying SNAP policy rules that QC is checking against ARE covered in the OLG: the $125 earned income change reporting threshold is on the 'Change Reporting – Overview' page (Income-Related Changes section), income averaging policy is on the 'Types of Earned Income' page (Income Averaging section), prospective income calculation is covered in BEACON procedures on the 'Entering, Changing, and Ending Earned Income in BEACON' page (Prospective Tab), and terminated income handling is addressed on the 'Simplified Reporting – Recertification' page. The FNS section's specific procedural details (e.g., QC must use the most recently calculated average, QC must correct misapplications, the three-way routing of reported/unreported sources to sub-sections) are QC review steps with no caseworker equivalent.
